title: Bioelectric changes let wild-type planaria grow other species' head shapes in days

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Bioelectric changes let wild-type planaria grow other species' head shapes in days

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Head shapes of existing planarian species are readily recapitulated by genetically wild-type planaria whose bioelectric circuit is altered during regeneration, so 100–150 million years of evolutionary distance in morphospace can be crossed in a few days through the dynamics of bioelectric pattern memories.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Bioelectric networks as reprogrammable interface to morphogenetic capabilities

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Indeed, it has been shown that existing planarian species’ head shapes are readily recapitulated by a genetically wild-type animal experiencing changes to its bioelectric circuit during regeneration—100–150 million years of evolutionary distance in morphospace can be crossed in a few days because of the dynamics of bioelectric pattern memories [197, 198].

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology”, Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS (2023), doi:10.1007/s00018-023-04790-z; section “Bioelectric networks as reprogrammable interface to morphogenetic capabilities”. Scope: Planarians (e.g. Girardia dorotocephala) treated with gap-junction blockers during regeneration

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-agential-13: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The morphological resemblance and lack of genetic change are testable with images and sequence data. The stronger assertion about traversing morphospace and bioelectric pattern memory is only indirectly supported.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Use blinded geometric morphometrics to compare treated regenerated heads with untreated conspecifics and reference species, alongside genotyping and voltage measurements. Clustering of treated heads with other species more strongly than with controls supports phenocopy, while the evolutionary-distance interpretation requires a phylogeny.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Drug effects may be nonspecific.

Two-dimensional head shape may not capture species identity.

The phrase 'crossed evolutionary distance' is metaphorical rather than a trajectory.

fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.72
discriminating power: 0.68
operationalizability: 0.88

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Shape distance and divergence time are both measurable, and TimeTree can check the temporal clause once the species pair is fixed. The shape data are the published images from one experiment, not an open landmark file, so an independent remasurement is limited. Species-specific recapitulation has to be separated from nonspecific disruption.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify head outlines of gap-junction-blocker-treated genetically wild-type Girardia dorotocephala and compute morphological distances to untreated heads of other planarian species, then place those species on a dated phylogeny. Treated heads falling nearer other species' shapes than their own controls, across divergence times on the order of 100 to 150 million years, would support the report; shapes that are only disrupted, or divergence times far from that range for the species actually compared, would count against the corresponding clause.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A generic dysmorphic head can be scored as species-like unless the distance to each species shape is pre-specified.

Head-shape measurements live in the 2015 paper's figures, not in TimeTree or a morphometric archive.
